event.summary: Residual switch wording does not change the restart contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: One old migration paragraph retains obsolete switch wording, but the changed contract and shipped Restart path unconditionally use terminal hosts. Details: SPEC_impl.md:2488-2492 says 'with the internal switch on, a Restart ... starts the new launch in a terminal host'. This residual clause is imprecise after removal, but SPEC_impl.md:2294 explicitly establishes 'A supervisor creates every terminal in a terminal host; nothing selects tmux', and 2289-2292 says 'Every create, tab open and Restart makes a host terminal'. The dispatcher at crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/core.rs:12942-13018 distinguishes host versus tmux only for existing-agent evidence and migration; it has no substrate selector and unconditionally settles host starts before the launch. The initial concern was a misleading maintenance contract, not changed runtime behavior or a user instruction to perform a harmful action. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed minor residual wording; not reported as a substantive security/correctness defect. proposed_drop: exact basis is the explicit unconditional contract quoted above and matching dispatcher, which resolve the apparent conditional. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; no security, data-loss or process-loss route established or suspected from this wording. Source-only conclusion; no execution. This revises and closes lead f1.

event.summary: Remove the obsolete condition from the migration contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The authoritative instructions for moving an existing session to a new terminal still say Restart requires an internal switch that this change removes. A maintainer following that migration paragraph is given a nonexistent prerequisite and an incorrect description of when migration happens. Details: SPEC_impl.md:2488-2492 retains 'with the internal switch on, a Restart ... starts the new launch in a terminal host'. Attribution checked against the parent: identical wording was at parent SPEC_impl.md:2504-2508 and was valid there, because parent :2295-2333 defined SupervisorSeams::new_terminals and explicitly allowed Restart to remain in tmux with it off. This commit removes that selector, changes the assigned Every new terminal in a host and Creating agents in hosts paragraphs (:2294-2320), and even removes the same switch condition from Clone/Replace later in this migration paragraph (:2555), but leaves its opening conditional intact. The core.rs diff removes 'let into_host = host_agent || self.new_terminals() == NewTerminals::Host' and makes host settling unconditional (reviewed source :12973-12981); the new-host path therefore has no condition corresponding to the retained instruction. The root contract declares SPEC_impl.md authoritative for implementation choices, so correct nearby paragraphs expose the contradiction rather than refute it. Fix by making this paragraph's Restart/migration statement unconditional as the implementation and the other changed paragraphs already are. Suggested bucket: other, a documentation correctness defect; no shipped runtime divergence or security/data-loss route is established. Confidence: confirmed from parent/reviewed source and patch; no execution. proposed_drop: false. The earlier proposal to drop as minor or resolved by nearby correct statements is withdrawn; preserve its original consequence of misleading maintenance/migration instructions, without upgrading to hypothetical runtime harm. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no established or suspected route from this wording. This closes the synthesis lead under the original ID.

event.summary: Offline uninstall can leave an old tmux server by explicit contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 500548b9253b07a26fd03119679184b69544e31d. TLDR: Uninstall may leave an earlier release's private tmux server running if it had already outlived its stopped supervisor. Details: source inspection of crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/backend.rs:3260-3360 confirms stop_supervisor checks ActiveState, skips systemctl stop for inactive/failed units, then explicitly ends terminal hosts only; no old tmux cleanup remains. This can leave old terminals/processes on an offline retry. The assigned product contract explicitly accepts this: SPEC.md:214-219 says 'Uninstall has no tmux step of its own: stopping the supervisor’s service ends whatever still runs under it, an earlier release’s private tmux server included, but one that outlived a supervisor stopped before uninstall (on a host never updated to a release that ends it at startup, say) keeps running, which the maintainer accepted on 2026-11-11.' SPEC_impl.md:7860-7863 likewise names the startup-failure plus later-stop route and accepts it. Suggested bucket: high if not accepted, since incomplete uninstall leaves resource usage and unreachable old terminals; other as a deliberate residual, not a reported defect. Confidence: confirmed source behavior and explicit acceptance. proposed_drop: exact acceptance quoted above. possible_cover: none; no coverage files searched. Could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work or security route from leaving these same-account processes alive; removal does not itself kill them. The existing confirmation-time activity checks still govern connected uninstall, and source-only inspection does not establish an additional destructive route. No runtime observations.

event.summary: Check legacy-retry rollback wording against allocated checkouts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The newly added contract may promise rolling back an interrupted old-terminal create even when its earlier attempt allocated a managed checkout that source deliberately retains with an error session. Details: assigned SPEC_impl.md Creating agents in hosts newly says a tmux retry claimed by takeover is 'refused before anything starts and rolled back like a launch whose spec never landed'. Previously inspected core.rs:15866-15924 distinguishes no-origin/planned rollback from an allocated or unreadable fresh origin, retained as a visible error to preserve ownership. Discovery check needed: exact wording and surrounding global creation/rollback contract, including what 'like a launch whose spec never landed' already encompasses, before concluding an independent documentation mismatch. Suggested bucket: other for potentially misleading maintenance/visible-error contract; no established runtime bug. Confidence: unresolved source/contract lead. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: supplied interface g107/g107-l3 concerns retained private launch artifacts after removed-row retry, a different consequence; no duplicate inferred. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; the implementation retains ownership rather than deleting allocated work. Source-only; no reproduction or execution.

event.summary: Legacy retry uses the referenced spec-write failure policy
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The new old-terminal-retry sentence uses 'rolled back like a launch whose spec never landed' as a reference to an existing failure policy; that policy already preserves a session owning an allocated checkout. The suspected missing-exception documentation defect is not established. Original concern preserved: a reader treating 'rolled back' as unconditional row deletion could expect no session when a retained error session actually appears. Checks/results: exact assigned text at SPEC_impl.md:2315-2319 compares the refusal with spec-not-landed cleanup, rather than explicitly promising deletion of every row or checkout. The complete Owned checkout admission and lifetime subsection's governing allocation paragraph (:4120-4125) expressly says 'A post-allocation failure atomically retains an error session and membership instead of losing the only deletion handle.' Product SPEC.md:1756-1762 says 'Once allocation has occurred, failures retain the session and its checkout association for inspection and Delete.' Source at core.rs:11827-11863 confirms that the referenced FailedStart::Spec policy deletes ordinary pre-effect rows but calls retain_create_refusal for allocated checkouts; the new refuse_retried_tmux_launch at :15866-15924 applies exactly that same distinction, rolling back only no-origin or Planned origins and retaining allocated or unreadable origins. Thus the referenced policy and its explicit governing exception agree; unlike f1, there is no removed prerequisite or false runtime condition here. Suggested bucket if the suspected wording defect existed: other; no user-work or security route established, and the actual implementation preserves checkout ownership. Confidence: confirmed source/contract refutation of a distinct mismatch; no execution. proposed_drop: exact cross-reference meaning plus the explicit allocation exceptions quoted above, not mere correct production behavior or low severity. possible_cover: supplied g107/g107-l3 concerns the separate leftover private-artifact timing after a removed-row refusal and does not refute or establish this wording concern. Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/loss-of-work route from this sentence; do not interpret the wording as authorization to delete an allocated checkout contrary to the explicit governing contract. This closes lead f3 without a new verified or unverified finding. Parent owns disposition; no proposed drop is assumed accepted.
